metadata.title: Claude, Oversimplified
metadata.purpose: Give a total beginner a working mental model of Claude — three surfaces, three tiers, three vocabulary words, five prompting rules, and the expert-mode unlock of Skills plus Projects.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro) — durations are word-count estimates until GATE 0 audio lock

beats.narration_text: Hola. This is Liam, in for Bear. Someone asked Claude: what is the fastest way to understand how Claude actually works? Here's what that looks like — a two-minute map of the whole thing, so you never feel lost again.

props.ask: What is the fastest way to understand how Claude actually works?
props.answer_preview: Claude runs in three places and three tiers…
props.command: Someone asked Claude: what is the fastest way to understand how Claude actually works?

beats.narration_text: Claude lives in three places. Browser — you type, it answers, no install. Desktop app — same account, but now it can see your local files and unlocks Chat, Cowork, and Code. And Cowork — that's Claude running for minutes at a time on a real task while you step away.

illustration.concept: Three-layer stack diagram: Browser at bottom, Desktop in middle, Cowork at top — each level adds a capability badge (files, autonomous work). Simple hand-drawn style.
illustration.layout: Vertical stack, left-aligned labels, capability badges on the right of each layer

beats.narration_text: Three tiers. Free tier — browser only, good for two weeks of testing. Pro tier — Cowork, Code, Projects, best model. Max tier — heavy daily use without hitting the ceiling. Pick the tier that matches how often you reach for it.

card.sub: Free to test. Pro to work. Max to never stop.

beats.narration_text: Three words you need. Token — the unit Claude thinks in; a page is roughly five hundred of them. Cowork — Claude doing the work while you do something else. Claude Code — Claude inside your terminal, built for developers. Everything else is vocabulary you can learn later.

card.sub: The only three words that matter before week one.

beats.narration_text: Five prompting rules. Be specific — vague input, vague output. Give examples — paste something you like and say write like this. Say what you want, not what you don't. Start short, then add detail. And when the conversation gets confused, open a fresh chat. These five rules beat any prompt template.

illustration.concept: Five numbered rules arranged as a hand-drawn checklist on a cream card — each rule has a 3-4 word label and a short contrasting bad/good example phrase beneath it.
illustration.layout: Single-column numbered list, terracotta checkboxes on the left, bad example struck through, good example clean

beats.narration_text: Expert mode is Skills plus Projects. Skills are reusable prompts you trigger with a slash command — type /negotiation and Claude runs your full playbook. Projects are persistent contexts — upload everything about a client once and every chat inside remembers. That combination is how pros make Claude feel like a dedicated employee.

card.sub: Slash commands recall your playbooks. Projects keep your context alive.

beats.narration_text: Your move this week. Pick one thing you keep doing manually — a summary, a draft, a meeting recap — and run it through Claude right now. Don't overthink the prompt. Start with two sentences. See what comes back. That first honest test is worth more than any guide you could read.

card.copy: Run one real task in Claude today
card.sub: Two sentences is enough. React to the output. Improve from there.

beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. Claude, Oversimplified. Three surfaces, three tiers, three words, five rules, and one expert unlock. That is everything a beginner needs to stop feeling lost.

card.sub: this is Liam, in for Bear

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you're explaining Claude to someone who has never used it. Ask Claude to give you the oversimplified version — not what it can do (too long), but the one mental model that predicts when Claude will work well versus when it won't, and one concrete example that shows the model in action.
